question: A 30-year-old woman is diagnosed with genital tuberculosis. HSG shows bilateral cornual block. She is started on standard 6-month ATT (2HRZE/4HR). After completing treatment, she asks about her chances of natural conception. What is the most accurate counselling?

answers.text: ATT will clear the infection, and the tubal obstruction is expected to resolve over the following 3–6 months, restoring natural fertility

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. This is the most common misconception about genital TB management. ATT eradicates the active bacillary infection but does NOT reverse the structural damage — the fibrosis, adhesions, and tubal obstruction are permanent. Telling a patient her tubes will open after treatment is inaccurate and harmful.

answers.text: ATT will cure the active infection, but bilateral tubal block from fibrosis is irreversible; natural conception is very unlikely and IVF is the only realistic option for biological parenthood

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. This is the key clinical principle: ATT cures the bacillary infection but the structural damage (fibrosis, luminal obstruction, Asherman syndrome from endometrial TB) is irreversible. Women with bilateral cornual block after genital TB have very poor prognosis for natural conception, and IVF (often with low success rates due to poor endometrial receptivity) is the only assisted reproductive option.

answers.text: ATT is not indicated once bilateral tubal block is confirmed, as the damage is already done and treatment offers no benefit

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. ATT must still be given to eradicate active infection, prevent disease progression (e.g., to peritoneum, other organs), reduce infectivity, and prevent reactivation. The fact that structural damage is irreversible does not negate the need for full ATT.

answers.text: Tubal reconstructive surgery after completing ATT can reliably restore tubal patency and natural fertility in the majority of cases

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Tubal reconstructive surgery for TB-damaged tubes has very poor outcomes due to the extensive intratubal fibrosis and endothelial damage. Unlike post-chlamydial peritubal adhesions (where adhesiolysis can sometimes restore function), TB causes transmural tubal destruction. IVF rather than surgical reconstruction is recommended.

overallFeedback.feedback: The cardinal principle: ATT cures the bacillary infection but CANNOT reverse fibrosis or tubal obstruction. Bilateral cornual block → IVF is the only assisted reproductive option, with poor prognosis due to endometrial damage.
Correct. ATT = infection cure; structural damage (bilateral tubal block, Asherman syndrome) = irreversible. IVF is the only realistic path to biological parenthood, with guarded prognosis.
